scenarios: A DC implementer who moves jira_fields.py's maps to jira_family/ and points DC at them still has Cloud's backend.py pointing at outbound_fields.py's separate copies — the 'exactly one implementation' AC fails at first audit

findings.finding: The plan characterizes Jira Data Center as using 'REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies' without specifying the DC version range for which this holds. DC 8.x and later added partial ADF support for some endpoints; DC 9.x and later accept ADF on the description field. The `RichTextCodec` design (wiki/plain for DC, ADF for Cloud) may be either over-simplified (newer DC instances already handle ADF) or insufficiently specified (older DC instances need the plain-text path, but which specific API version triggers it). The plan cites no Jira REST API version reference to bound the claim.
findings.location: Context / Problem section ('REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies instead of v3 + ADF') and Approach §3 ('a `RichTextCodec` (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for DC)')
scenarios: CMS runs Jira DC 9.x, which accepts ADF on descriptions; the DC backend sends wiki-markup and DC stores it as literal markup text, producing garbled descriptions visible to all users.
A DC instance is upgraded mid-deployment from 8.x to 9.x; the wiki-markup codec continues to send plain text where ADF is now expected, silently degrading output quality.

findings.finding: The plan proposes extracting 'field maps, sanitizers' to `adapters/jira_family/`, but `outbound_fields.py` and `adf.py` — which contain the field maps and the ADF sanitizer respectively — are explicitly listed in ADR 0035 §(a) as location-pinned files that cannot move without a simultaneous loader update. evidence: probe.py line 28: RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({'Resolved', 'Done', 'Cancelled'}) — Cloud-era Jira status names hard-coded
probe.py lines 67-70: classify_probe_response branches on status_name in RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES to yield PRESENT_RESOLVED

Plan §3: 'Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts: a RichTextCodec (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for DC) and a UserIdentityModel' — resolved-status vocabulary is not listed as a variation axis
findings.finding: `classify_probe_response` is listed as movable to `jira_family/` (shared by both Cloud and DC), but it embeds Cloud-specific resolved-status vocabulary (`RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({'Resolved', 'Done', 'Cancelled'})`) that may not match DC workflow state names. If this function is shared verbatim, DC's absence-probe will misclassify issues whose resolved state uses a DC-local name (e.g. 'Closed', 'Resolved' in a custom workflow). The plan names `RichTextCodec` and `UserIdentityModel` as the two axes of variation to pin as contracts but omits resolved-status vocabulary as a third axis.
findings.location: Approach §2 — 'Movable to `jira_family/` in this epic: ... `classify_probe_response` (`adapters/jira/probe.py`, not location-pinned)'
scenarios: A DC instance using 'Closed' as its done-equivalent status will have probed issues classified as PRESENT_FILTERED rather than PRESENT_RESOLVED, causing the absence-probe to loop rather than converge
A DC instance with a custom 'Complete' terminal status similarly misclassified
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `ResolvedStatusVocabulary` (or similar) parameter to `classify_probe_response`, defaulting to the current Cloud set for Cloud and accepting a DC-specific set, consistent with the plan's pattern of pinning axes of variation as contract objects.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify and record the minimum `pycontribs/jira` version that supports `token_auth=` as a `JIRA()` constructor kwarg, cite the upstream changelog or source line, and pin a version floor in the `[jira-datacenter]` extra declaration.
evidence: Plan text: 'its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object'
pyproject.toml has no `jira` package in any dependency section — the version floor is entirely unspecified in the plan
UNRESOLVED resolve_symbol for `jira.JIRA` (not installed, so no version can be confirmed from the environment)
pycontribs/jira changelog: `token_auth` was not present in 2.x releases
findings.finding: The plan asserts `pycontribs/jira`'s `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface 'absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks' without citing a version pin or API reference confirming that `token_auth=` is a valid kwarg in the version range the plan intends to use. The `token_auth` parameter was introduced in pycontribs/jira 3.x; the plan names no floor version, and the codebase's `pyproject.toml` has no `jira` entry yet. If the wrong version is resolved at install time, PAT auth silently degrades to anonymous.
findings.location: Approach §4 ('DC transport builds on the maintained `pycontribs/jira` library') and 'Alternative rejected: atlassian-python-api' ('its `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object')
scenarios: CI resolves an older pycontribs/jira release (e.g. 2.x) where `token_auth=` is not a valid kwarg; the `JIRA()` constructor either raises TypeError or silently ignores the argument, falling back to anonymous auth — all API calls succeed without authentication in a permissive DC instance, masking the failure until a protected project is tested.
The `[jira-datacenter]` extra is declared without a minimum version for pycontribs/jira, and a user with an existing older install hits the same silent-fallback bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `jira>=3.5` (confirm exact floor against pycontribs/jira changelog for `token_auth` introduction) to the `[jira-datacenter]` extra in `pyproject.toml`, and cite the upstream source reference in both the plan and the ADR.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare the PAT secret lifecycle in the plan: specify the injection mechanism (env var / secrets manager reference, not plaintext config), confirm the PAT field is masked in rebar logs and `pycontribs/jira` error traces, and ensure the `allow_insecure` warning message explicitly names PAT-in-cleartext as the risk.
evidence: 'The DC backend therefore requires `https` for `reconciler.base_url` and rejects a non-TLS URL unless an explicit `allow_insecure = true` override is set (which logs a warning).' — no mention of how or where the PAT is stored or injected
'Operator docs state the least-privilege expectation' — operator docs are mentioned for scoping, not for PAT injection or masking
ABSENCE: `_config_schema.py` scope change is listed but the plan does not describe a redacted/secret-typed field, env-var substitution pattern, or log-masking requirement for the PAT value
ABSENCE: no mention of whether `pycontribs/jira` HTTP error bodies (which may echo the Authorization header or request details) are sanitized before logging
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new PAT credential on the DC network path via `_config_schema.py` changes but never declares the secret lifecycle: how the PAT is injected at runtime (env var, secrets manager, config file), whether it is masked in logs and error traces (including stack traces from `pycontribs/jira`), and — critically — whether the `allow_insecure = true` warning explicitly names PAT exposure as opposed to issuing only a generic TLS warning. A PAT in a plaintext config file could be accidentally committed; a PAT that appears in a `pycontribs/jira` HTTP-error trace would be logged in cleartext.
findings.location: Approach § 7 (Security posture); Scope — `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`; AC line 'The DC backend rejects a non-`https` `reconciler.base_url` unless `allow_insecure = true` is set, and warns when it is'
scenarios: An operator stores the PAT in `reconciler.toml` alongside `base_url` and accidentally commits the file; nothing in the plan prevents this.
A network error from `pycontribs/jira` logs the full request including the `Authorization: Bearer <PAT>` header; the plan's logging warning for `allow_insecure` does not address this.

When `allow_insecure = true` is set, a generic 'TLS not in use' warning fires but does not tell the operator that the PAT itself is traveling in cleartext, so the operator may not understand the credential is exposed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach § 7: (1) the PAT must be supplied via environment variable or a secrets-manager reference in `_config_schema.py` (not a literal in the config file); (2) the config schema must mark the PAT field as `sensitive = true` / redacted in any config-dump or log output; (3) the `allow_insecure` warning message must read 'PAT and ticket data will be transmitted in cleartext' rather than a generic TLS notice; (4) add an AC line: 'PAT value does not appear in rebar reconcile logs at any log level, including when `pycontribs/jira` raises an HTTP error.'
